method: Evidence/rights gates first. Placement blends interest, relevance, novelty, familiarity, consequence, source confidence, originality, visual strength, freshness, radar context and rotation pressure, then applies a diversity rerank so nearby homepage slots prefer different categories and subjects. Editorial story-overrides are applied before ranking so approved headlines and imagery persist across generated homepage surfaces.

feature.headline: Nationalist conference moved to Burlington after two Hamilton venues cancelled bookings
feature.deck: DomCon 2026 was held at The Atrium on North Service Road. The private venue says it did not know the Dominion Society's background when it accepted the booking.
feature.label: Local affairs
feature.alt: Graphic showing DomCon moving along the QEW from two cancelled Hamilton venues to Burlington.
feature.storyGoal: Explain how DomCon relocated from two cancelled Hamilton bookings to a private Burlington venue and identify the unanswered questions about the booking and notice.

feature.headline: Burlington tested curbside recycling before the blue box. The result looked like a failure.
feature.deck: No bins, four sorted streams and 1,000 homes exposed the problem that volunteers alone could not solve.
feature.label: Local history
feature.alt: A 1970s kitchen counter with a glass jar, metal can, newspapers and sorting bags, with Burlington homes beyond the window.
feature.storyGoal: Reconstruct Burlington's 1971 curbside recycling experiment and explain why weak weekly set-out numbers concealed much broader participation and a lesson about the public infrastructure recycling would require.

feature.headline: Which Burlington intersection is actually the worst?
feature.deck: The public records point to a larger problem along one of Burlington's busiest roads.
feature.label: Road safety
feature.alt: Illustration of a damaged car and motorcycle at an intersection; not a photograph of a collision discussed in this article.
feature.storyGoal: Use collision counts, red-light camera totals and engineering records to explain why Burlington's worst intersection changes by the measure used, and why different problems keep appearing along Guelph Line.

feature.headline: Why do cars appear to roll uphill on Burlington's King Road?
feature.deck: For decades, one short stretch of King Road has made Burlington drivers question which way is down. The explanation is stranger than a hidden magnet.
feature.label: Local mysteries
feature.alt: A car travelling along the wooded section of King Road in Burlington near the area known for its magnetic hill.
feature.storyGoal: Start with the apparent gravity-defying motion on King Road, trace the decades-old Burlington legend, and reveal the visual-perception mechanism only after the mystery has been established.

feature.headline: Four Burlington technologies that ended up around the world
feature.deck: Four Burlington operations make things most residents will never see, even though their work shows up far beyond the city.
feature.label: Made in Burlington
feature.alt: Illustration linking Burlington to water, laboratory, broadcast and bio-based technologies around the world.
feature.storyGoal: Show Burlington's global technology footprint through four verified examples whose products or systems are used around the world.

rail.headline: Can you have a backyard fire pit in Burlington?
rail.deck: The answer changes depending on what you burn, what you burn it in and where in Burlington you live.
rail.label: Home rules
rail.alt: Illustration comparing a wood fire pit with a propane fire table in a Burlington backyard.
rail.storyGoal: Explain the Burlington backyard-fire rule in plain language, including the urban wood-fire ban, cooking exception, propane and natural-gas exception, and rural permit system.

rail.headline: Five creepiest Burlington mysteries
rail.deck: A child vanished 400 yards from home. A dinner in Niagara Falls ended with no trace. Some of Burlington's strangest questions are still open.
rail.label: Local mysteries
rail.alt: A dark waterfront scene used as an illustration for Burlington mysteries.
rail.storyGoal: Tell five verified Burlington mystery stories with narrative tension while clearly separating open police cases from folklore and never presenting speculation as fact.

rail.headline: The least expensive complete lunches we found in Burlington
rail.deck: We checked current restaurant menus and recent reviews to see how far $11 still goes at Burlington lunch spots.
rail.label: Food & drink
rail.alt: A sandwich, soup and drink arranged as an inexpensive lunch.
rail.storyGoal: Find the lowest currently verifiable Burlington lunch prices that still buy a main plus at least one meaningful side, bread, soup, salad or drink.

latest.alt: Flooding in Burlington during a major rain event.
latest.storyGoal: Explain what Burlington's more than $90 million in stormwater investment has physically changed, using Tuck Creek as a concrete example while being explicit about unfinished and paused work.
